context.firstUser: A teacher, streamer, or group host who has just completed a fair random draw on iPhone or iPad.
context.primaryJob: Make the selected contestant unmistakable, exciting, and easy to continue from without obscuring the result.
context.desiredResponse: A high-energy shared celebration that still preserves the winner name, number, and next actions at a glance.
referenceProducts: Jackbox Games — room-scale winner reveals with a single unmistakable result
Kahoot! — celebratory educational feedback with immediate next-step controls
Duolingo — playful character-led rewards that remain legible and task-focused

blurTest.evidence: The winner number and name remain the dominant central mass on both phone and tablet, with the headline and actions forming a clear secondary hierarchy.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The framed result card, giant numbered badge, confetti field, and animated hero create a recognizable game-show reveal rather than a generic modal.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: The rendered views immediately communicate winner number 7, Julia Wolk, a celebration state, Keep Going, and Reset Picks.

realityTest.evidence: The fixture uses the same numbered contestant model, production fonts, responsive layout, bundled animation assets, and native controls as the shipping app.

journeyTest.evidence: The state provides a prominent winner, a non-destructive continuation path, an explicit reset path, and a close control without exposing the underlying reset controls.

platformTest.evidence: Fresh simulator renders were inspected at original resolution on a NameSnap iPhone 17 Pro and iPad Pro 13-inch, including safe areas and tablet-specific composition.

buyerValueTest.evidence: The celebration materially upgrades the shared picking moment with 50 visual combinations, varied licensed audio, haptics, confetti, and clear continuation controls.

implementationTest.evidence: The Debug simulator build succeeds, raster and GIF assets load from the app bundle, reduced-motion behavior is defined, and the final iPhone and iPad pixels were inspected after the tablet overlap repair.

screenFindings.finding: The compact composition reserves the top of the card for the illustrated guitarist, keeps the winner result fully visible, and presents two large touch targets without exposing underlying controls.
The tablet composition centers the entire result and keeps the animated hero behind the card edges, preserving the complete long winner name and both actions.

repairs: Loaded standalone raster celebration files through Bundle paths after the first rendered phone pass exposed a missing hero image.
Moved hard shadows to card surfaces after the first pass revealed duplicated-looking text.
Reserved additional compact header space and hid the underlying reset controls while the winner overlay is active.
Rejected the first iPad render because the foreground guitarist obscured the winner name, then moved tablet heroes behind the result card and re-rendered successfully.
verdict: PASS — build 18's winner celebration is clear, high-energy, responsive, and visually verified on both iPhone and iPad after repairing the tablet overlap.
